blogs.title: Neck Swelling That Won’t Shrink: Dermatomyositis on the Radar
blogs.description: Explore how an adult male’s neck edema, initially misdiagnosed as Ludwig’s angina or idiopathic angioedema, was actually dermatomyositis. This post outlines the ED diagnostic pitfalls, key red flags that should trigger a CK test, the value of imaging, and why a high index of suspicion is essential in unexplained neck swelling with subtle skin changes.

blogs.title: The Anti‑SAE1 Story: Why One Autoantibody Can Change Your Plan
blogs.description: Anti‑SAE1 antibodies are rare but profoundly influence dermatomyositis management. We review their epidemiology, typical clinical hooks—dysphagia, interstitial lung disease, and heightened malignancy risk—how their detection guides prognosis and surveillance, and the therapeutic implications for corticosteroids, immunosuppressants and biologic agents.

blogs.title: When ENT Meets Immunology: A Multidisciplinary Playbook for Dermatomyositis in the ED
blogs.description: Managing neck swelling that threatens the airway requires close collaboration between ENT, emergency, and rheumatology. This article walks through airway assessment, the crucial role of prompt IV steroids, avoiding unnecessary antibiotics, and coordinating rapid immunology consults to streamline care and prevent delays.

blogs.title: From Steroids to Rituximab: Building a Stepwise Prescription for Dermatomyositis
blogs.description: Optimal treatment of dermatomyositis remains evolving. Here we present a pragmatic algorithm: high‑dose IV methylprednisolone → oral prednisone taper → steroid‑sparring agents (mycophenolate, azathioprine) → IVIG or rituximab in refractory or fulminant disease. We discuss dosing, infection prophylaxis, monitoring, and adjustments in the setting of interstitial lung disease.

blogs.title: Skimming the Skin: Nailfold Capillaries to Gottron Papules, How to Spot Dermatomyositis Early
blogs.description: Early recognition hinges on catching subtle skin clues. This post reviews periungual erythema, Holstein sign, heliotrope rash, and Gottron papules, and shows how a focused skin exam and nailfold capillaroscopy can expedite a dermatomyositis diagnosis. Practical visual cues and quick examination tips are provided for busy clinicians.
